title: Gideon and the Orbit
premise: Ada Iversen, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Perihelion, has survived three years of war by staying invisible—until the freighter Vesper returns from a deep-space jump with its crew aged backward into children, carrying a message that could end the war or ignite its final phase. Hunted by both warring factions who want the message destroyed, Ada must shepherd the child-crew and the message through contested orbits to the neutral assembly at Ceres, discovering along the way that the message is a confession implicating her own former employers in starting the war. In the end, Ada chooses to broadcast the truth openly rather than trade it for safety, sacrificing her invisibility—and nearly her life—to finally belong to something larger than herself.
about_author: Mirabel Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that never saw each other. She writes about lonely people holding fragile lines of connection across vast distances.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Establishes her solitary routine aboard the Perihelion: hauling cargo drones, maintaining automated systems, avoiding both fleets' traffic lanes. A near-miss with a patrol frigate reminds her how thin her invisibility really is. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort and cost of being no one.

chapters.title: Signal from Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The station's sensors catch an impossible return vector—a ship emerging from a dead zone where nothing should survive. Ada debates whether to report it, knowing any contact makes her visible. She logs it quietly and preps a docking cradle, telling herself it's just protocol. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Children of the Vesper
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Vesper docks crewed entirely by children wearing adult-rated vacsuits—the original crew aged backward by whatever happened in the deep field. Their captain, eleven-year-old Sef Okafor, still speaks with an old man's cadence. Ada realizes they remember everything. Emotional beat: uncanny grief, tenderness toward strangers.

chapters.title: What the Deep Field Did
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Flashback woven through present dialogue: the Vesper's jump through an experimental corridor, the reversal, the deaths of those too old to survive reversion. Sef explains they carry a sealed message from the expedition's lead scientist—one both governments will kill to suppress. Emotional beat: a child bearing an adult's burden.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Beacon
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Both warring factions ping the station within hours; someone leaked the Vesper's return. Ada must choose: hand over the message, destroy it, or run. She loads the children and the data core onto her hauler and burns for the outer lanes. Emotional beat: the end of hiding, chosen under duress.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest: One War
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Aboard the hauler, the child-crew struggles with bodies that can't reach the controls their minds remember. Ada improvises rigging and routines; grudging trust forms. Sef tests Ada's motives, suspecting she'll sell them out. Emotional beat: fragile interdependence becoming something like family.

chapters.title: The Toll at Juno Gate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At a checkpoint, Ada bribes an old acquaintance, dockmaster Rhee, for clean transponders—but Rhee recognizes the Vesper's signature and demands the message as payment. Ada refuses; they escape on a slingshot trajectory that damages the hauler's heat sinks. Emotional beat: loyalty costing more than betrayal would.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Pursuing faction agents board via a maintenance umbilical during repairs. Sef stalls them with a child's performance of confusion while Ada vents the compartment. One agent, Corporal Vashti, hesitates before evacuating—she's seen the deep-field project files. Emotional beat: enemies who might not be enemies.

chapters.title: Decryption
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. With breathing room, Ada and Sef open fragments of the message: coordinates, research logs, and a partial confession naming Meridian Combine—the corporation that once employed Ada—as architect of the corridor experiment and the war's true instigator. Ada recognizes names. Emotional beat: the past she fled reaching out to claim her.

chapters.title: Ada Iversen, Employee 4471
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, heavy flashback. Three years ago Ada discovered anomalies in Meridian's shipping manifests and chose silence over whistleblowing, then ran when colleagues started disappearing. Her invisibility was never neutrality—it was complicity. She confesses this to Sef. Emotional beat: shame confronted, the theme of justice outside the law turned inward.

chapters.title: The Neutral Ground
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. They reach Ceres, where the war's stalled peace assembly convenes. But Meridian's lobbyists control access, and both delegations have warrants for 'salvage recovery' of the Vesper. An old friend of Sef's late captain offers shelter in the ring's undercity. Emotional beat: sanctuary that feels like a trap.

chapters.title: Undercity Bargains
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. To reach the assembly floor, they need a delegate's credentials. Ada trades her only leverage—her Meridian access codes—to a fixer named Okonjo, knowing it marks her permanently in every database. For the first time in three years, she exists on paper. Emotional beat: trading anonymity for agency.

chapters.title: Vashti's Dossier
chapters.summary: Corporal Vashti's POV. The agent, reassigned to Ceres security, has been quietly assembling proof of Meridian's role but lacks the courage—or the catalyst—to act. She intercepts Ada, not to arrest her but to compare files. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: a soldier choosing conscience over chain of command.

chapters.title: The Assembly Floor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Using Okonjo's credentials, Ada gains the gallery as delegates debate ceasefire terms built on Meridian-brokered 'neutrality.' She watches the corporation's director, Halvard Voss, steer negotiations toward a peace that buries the evidence forever. Emotional beat: seeing power work in daylight, smooth and rotten.

chapters.title: Sef Speaks
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef attempts to testify formally and is dismissed as a fabrication—an impossibility, a stunt. Security moves to detain the 'salvage property' of the Vesper. Ada pulls the fire alarm of the whole station: she hijacks the assembly's public address. Emotional beat: righteous fury, the moment retreat ends.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cornered in the transmission hub, Ada begins streaming the full decrypted confession to every band in the system rather than surrendering the core. Voss cuts power; Vashti holds the door against Meridian security. The children relay manual overrides only their reversed expertise can perform. Emotional beat: climax—allies holding the line while truth goes out unstoppable.

chapters.title: What Truth Costs
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The broadcast lands: fleets stand down mid-engagement, delegations fracture, Voss is arrested by his own security detail. But Ada took a round protecting the transmitter and lies critical in the undercity clinic. The system celebrates people the children barely know. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Long Recovery
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, drifting in and out of consciousness. Visitors: Vashti testifying before the tribunal, Okonjo erasing her debts, Rhee sending contraband fruit. Sef reads her the Vesper's log so she doesn't miss anything. Emotional beat: learning to be cared for after years of self-sufficiency.

chapters.title: Tribunal Testimony
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The child-crew testifies about the deep field; their testimony, once dismissed, now anchors the war-crimes proceedings. Sef chooses to tell the full truth, including the deaths they caused trying to protect the message. Emotional beat: justice that includes accountability, not just accusation.

chapters.title: Offers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Everyone wants something from her now: Meridian's successors want her silence, the tribunal wants her testimony, a shipping consortium wants a famous face. Ada realizes visibility is its own kind of cage. She declines all of it and asks instead one question: what happens to the Vesper's children? Emotional beat: refusing to be a symbol.

chapters.title: Crew Manifest, Amended
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The tribunal grants the child-crew guardianship arrangements of their own design; several choose each other over adult custodians. Sef asks Ada to sign on as the Vesper's civilian liaison—not guardian, crew. She says yes. Emotional beat: belonging offered plainly and accepted.

chapters.title: First Heading
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating short passages. The refitted Vesper departs Ceres on a humanitarian run—carrying supplies, testimony, and news to systems the war cut off. Ada at the console, Sef at the helm, no longer hiding in anyone's blind spots. Final image: a beacon left burning behind them for whoever comes next. Emotional beat: earned hope, connection sustained.
